refined.headline: Of the 14 h=20 relative labels, the DEV-only composite picks XR_neumom h=20, the per-date rank of a residual that also removes 12-1 momentum, trained on the continuous rank. Long top-20, step 5, 50 bps: DEV 30.9% vs a horizon-matched random 11.8% (excess +19.1%, NW t 4.25; averaged over all 5 entry phases +15.8%, t 4.11); 26.2% at 80 bps. The 2026 holdout is positive but weak: phase-averaged excess +3.9%/yr (t 0.60), 13.9% vs random 10.2%. The single-phase +9.2% (t 1.54) is the luckiest of the 5 phases. The robust choices are the 20-day hold and the beta/vol/size/momentum neutraliser, not the label form. RANK, 20/60/20 and top-30 binary are tied on DEV. A dedicated bottom-30 avoid classifier and the T50/T10 cuts are cliffs. 477 distinct DEV specs tried; best DEV t 4.25 vs Bonferroni 3.71 (3.91 counting round 1).

key_findings: Rank labels fix the event rate by design. Every h in {10,15,20} and every neutraliser gives +1 = 30.0% in every year, regime and month (monthly std 0.0001; corr with the Nifty month -0.12..+0.04). What moves is the liquidity-tercile mix (none 28.8/30.7/30.7 vs neu 29.3/30.9/29.9), the F&O sub-universe (-1 only 25.5%) and class churn (vs neu: neumom 3.5-3.8%, size 8.1-8.4%, none 10.8-11.0%).

Relative is not absolute. P(net>0 | +1) is 89-92% overall but 84-98% by year and falls to 37.9% in the worst month at h=20 (corr 0.42-0.64 with the Nifty month). P(net>0 | -1) is 2.9% in bull_up20 vs 17.4% in bear_dn20 windows.

Neutralisation removes the market-direction-dependent composition. Without it, the +1 class beta tilt is +0.09 z in up windows and -0.23 z in down windows (corr 0.60-0.67); with neu/neumom it is -0.04..-0.06 z (corr 0.06-0.16). neu still embeds the 12-1 momentum premium (+0.067 z); neumom removes it.

Horizon is decided by costs. h=10 has the most skill (phase-averaged DEV excess +23.8%, t 4.79), but DEV CAGR at 80 bps is 16.2% / 19.6% / 25.2% for h=10/15/20 and 2.6% / 10.2% / 17.7% at 130 bps. Any training horizon held 20 days earns +15..+18% DEV excess.
Neutraliser ranking neumom >= neu > none ~ size holds at h=10 and h=20 (phase-averaged DEV t at h=20: 4.11 / 3.81 / 3.27 / 2.90). none/size turn negative in 2026 (-7.7% / -1.8%).

Label form: continuous rank, 20/60/20 and top-30 binary are tied on DEV. 30/40/30 and 33/33/33 are slightly weaker. T10, T20, T50 and B30 are cliffs. Binary tail labels learn dispersion: B30 has the best bottom-30 AUC (0.572) but its avoid list outperformed in 2026 (+138 vs +84 bps); T30 loads on vol (R2 0.30).

Selected on DEV: h20_neumom_RANK. Long top-20 step 5 at 50 bps: DEV 30.9% vs random 11.8% (t 4.25; phase-averaged +15.8%, t 4.11), 26.2% at 80 bps, every DEV year positive. 2026: phase-averaged +3.9% (t 0.60), single-phase +9.2% (t 1.54), factor alpha +11.6% (t 1.78), 98th percentile of a persistence-matched null.
The asymmetry persists. Bottom-30 AUC is 0.538-0.557 DEV and about 0.555 in 2026 vs top-30 AUC of 0.516-0.521 DEV and 0.49-0.51 in 2026. The long books earn mostly by avoiding losers.

Avoid side: dropping the same score's bottom 10-30% adds +1.7..+3.8%/yr on DEV (t 3.4-3.8) and +1.3..+1.8% in 2026 (t 1.0-1.8), with factor-adjusted alpha +2.5% (t 3.7) in 2026. A plain 12-1 momentum avoid filter matches it on DEV (+3.7%, t 3.14) and beat it in 2026 (+5.4%).

Factor attribution: the neumom RANK long book has DEV alpha +17.4%/yr (t 3.99, R2 0.05), so it is not a boring tilt. No single-characteristic sort reaches it (best: 12-1 momentum +11.5%, t 1.62). 2026 was a factor storm (momentum LS +26%, vol +18%, trend +18%), and the neutral scores are short trend.

Phase luck: single-run S.compare holdout figures swing from -12.4% to +15.4% across the 10 calendar phases (neu RANK K20 s10). The selected model's default phase was the best of 5. Phase-averaged books are the robust statistic.

Luck calibration: an iid random picker has CAGR sd 1.9% on DEV. Constant per-stock random tilts have excess sd 6.7% DEV and NW t sd 1.37-1.54, reaching t 3.9 at the max of 40 draws. A persistence-matched null is calibrated (t sd about 1.05), and every top candidate sits 5.4-5.7 sd above it on DEV.

Sensitivity plateaus: K has a smooth slope (DEV excess +32/+19/+17/+12% for K=10/20/30/50, t 3.7-5.0, flat maxDD). Step 5 equals step 10 after phase-averaging. liq5 costs about 5 points of excess (t 4.25 to 3.28). Costs take about 1.5%/yr per +10 bps at h=20. 20-day name retention is 8-10%, so Sim's full round-trip charge is realistic for top-K books.

Variants: 75 label constructions screened, 23 walk-forward models, 477 distinct DEV specs at 50 bps (2088 DEV runs including cost and phase variants). Bonferroni one-sided 5% hurdle is t 3.71, or 3.91 adding round 1's ~600. The best DEV t (4.25) clears it narrowly; the choice among the top-3 forms is at noise level.
lab_issues_found: Calendar-phase sensitivity: Sim trades 1 of `step` phases, so single-run holdout excess varies from -12.4% to +15.4% across phases (neu RANK K20 s10, 2026). Recommend phase-averaged books (s7_phase.py) for every holdout claim.
Newey-West t is miscalibrated for persistent tilts: constant per-stock random scores give NW t sd 1.37 (DEV) / 1.54 (2026), max 3.9 in 40 draws. Use a persistence-matched null or a block bootstrap.

Sim charges a full round trip on re-picked names. That is fine for top-K books (8-10% 20-day retention) but understates absolute CAGR of avoid/EW books by up to about 6%/yr at 50 bps. Excess vs random-70% is unaffected.

Sim.run filters strategy candidates to finite score but not the random baseline. This is harmless for walk_forward2 scores but changes the universe for characteristic sorts with NaN (mom_12_1 is NaN on 11.8% of elig rows).
xs_metrics has no down-side AUC; the avoid side needs an inverted score and a bottom-class target. Suggest adding auc_down.
A rank label built on the full elig cross-section is 29.5/45/25.5, not 30/40/30, inside fno_proxy. Re-rank inside the traded universe when used as a target there.

The ranking cross-section is conditioned on survival: 1.0/1.6/2.1% of elig rows (h=10/15/20) hit a suspension, segment break or label_block within h days and are NaN. That is correct as a label, and Sim forced exits keep the investability numbers unbiased.
refined.recommendation: Primary selection label: XR_neumom at h=20. This is the per-date percentile rank of the OLS residual of per-date-winsorised open[t+1]->close[t+20] on [0.5*clip(beta_60,0,3)+0.5, vol_20, log_turn20, mom_12_1] over elig_base. Train on the continuous rank (LightGBM regression via walk_forward2). Treat the 20/60/20 and top-30 binary forms of the same residual as equivalent; an equal-weight rank ensemble of the three is the next step for R2_alpha. Avoid label: the bottom tail of the same score; drop the worst 10-30%, with the 10% cut the most robust in 2026. Do not train a dedicated bottom-30 classifier, which learns volatility, and do not use un-neutralised or size-only ranks. Execution: K=20 (10-30 is a plateau), 20-day hold, entries staggered daily or weekly to remove phase luck, liq2 universe, cost stress at 80/130 bps. Expected edge over a horizon-matched random book is about +4% (2026 phase-averaged) to +16%/yr (DEV), with random-like drawdowns (about -25 to -30%). Pair it with a separate regime/exposure layer if absolute drawdowns matter, and consider a 12-1 momentum avoid filter alongside the model's avoid list. Verdict: promising, not proven. The DEV edge is strong and clears Bonferroni narrowly; the 2026 holdout is positive but small once phase luck is removed.

refined.headline: Requiring both conditions doesn't help. The dual label (stock in the top-30% of XR_neu residual ranks AND absolute 20-day return above +50 bp) performs like a pure-relative label trained with the same loss (binary top-30%): +0.5%/yr on DEV, t 0.25, averaged over 5 signal-calendar phases, with no reduction in drawdown. The absolute leg makes the event rate move with the market: the daily +1 share correlates 0.70 with the market's return over the same window, and drops from 30% to 12% of names when the market falls more than 5% in the window. DUAL does beat the XR_neu regression by about 5%/yr, but that gain is a loss-function effect: the pure-relative binary model beats the regression by 4.6%/yr without any absolute leg. The best avoid rule is to drop the 30% of names with the lowest P(relative top-30): +3.3%/yr on DEV and +5.8%/yr in 2026, stable across phases. Avoid overlays built on a dedicated DUAL_down or REL_down model fail in 2026 (about -2.5%/yr).

key_findings: Event rates: adding the absolute leg (r>+50bp) to the top-30% residual label removes only 9.4% of +1 rows overall (2.3% in 2023 to 15.2% in 2022). The +1 share becomes market-dependent: daily corr 0.70 with the Nifty 500 return over the same window (REL 0.04, ABS 0.87). It is 29.7% in up windows, 23.3% in down windows and 11.9% when the window falls more than 5%. Monthly sd 4.2pp, minimum 11.4%.

Sensitivity map (tau 0-500bp x q 0.2/0.3/0.4 x h 10/20) is a smooth plateau with no cliffs. Raising tau or widening q always raises market dependence: at q=0.3, h=20, tau 0 to 500bp moves +1 from 27.6% to 22.7% and market corr from 0.67 to 0.83. h=10 behaves the same (11.1% of REL+1 removed).
Label/P&L coherence is mechanically perfect: DUAL +1 averages +1369bp net (100% hit), DUAL -1 averages -1038bp. That is conditioning on the outcome, not predictability.

Learnability: the DUAL model's per-date AUC on DUAL+1 is 0.545 DEV / 0.564 2026. The same-loss pure-relative binary model (M_RUP) scores 0.544 / 0.566 on the same event, and the two models' scores have rank correlation 0.90.

Investability, decisive same-loss test averaged over 5 signal-calendar phases: DUAL minus RUP is +0.5%/yr DEV (t 0.25, range -1.7 to +1.9) and +3.0%/yr 2026 (range -8.9 to +9.6). DUALP minus RUP is -4.6%/yr DEV (0/5 phases). No significant difference anywhere.
DUAL beats the XR_neu regression by about 5%/yr on DEV (8/8 K x step cells), but RUP beats it by 4.6%/yr (5/5 phases). The gain is from the binary top-tail loss, not the absolute leg.
Drawdowns: phase-mean DEV maxDD is REL -29.5%, RUP -31.0%, DUAL -32.3%, DUALP -31.8%. Book beta is 1.26 for REL and 1.33-1.35 for the top-tail books. The absolute leg does not cushion drawdowns.

Two-model alternatives fail. rank(REL)+rank(ABS) is +1.1%/yr DEV and -3.3% 2026 vs REL (0/8 holdout cells). P(top30) x P(abs) is -4.1%/yr DEV vs RUP. 'REL top-20 within ABS top half' is -0.8%/yr. The absolute model's extra content is market timing, which a fully invested cross-sectional book cannot use.

Input-side gate close>sma200 AND xr_mom60>0.7 (sample filter only): +0.9%/yr gate value on DEV (t 0.4); the model inside the gate is no better than on all of U, and retraining on the gate is worse. In 2026 the gate alone was worth +15.5%/yr (t 2.1). Not DEV-selectable; worth re-testing as a regime-dependent tilt.

Avoid side: the best overlay drops the 30% with the lowest P(relative top-30): +3.3%/yr DEV (t 4.6) and +5.8%/yr 2026 (t 6.0), phase-stable. Dedicated down models (DUAL_down, REL_down) classify well (AUC 0.556 in 2026) but fail as overlays in 2026 (-2.6%/yr, 0/5 phases), because the avoided names are high-vol residual losers with good raw returns in rebounds.

Phase noise: shifting the signal calendar by 0-4 days moves a top-20 book's 2026 CAGR by 10-14pp (e.g. REL 6.6-20.7%). A single-phase holdout difference of a few %/yr between label variants is not evidence.

Variants: 11 walk-forward models, 130 distinct DEV book configs, about 56 label variants screened on event rates. Under the null the expected max t is about 2.6 for 130 tries and about 3.2 for about 730 programme-wide. Relative-book DEV excess t of 3.0-4.0 only modestly clears this; DUAL-vs-relative paired t is at most about 1.
refined.recommendation: Don't add an absolute condition to the stock label. Use the pure-relative XR_neu residual rank at h=20 and train the selection model as a binary top-30% classifier (M_RUP), or rank-blend it with the XR_neu regression (SUM_REL_RUP: phase-mean 33.4% DEV, 19.1% in 2026 vs about 7% random). For avoiding names, drop the bottom 30% by P(relative top-30): +3.3%/yr DEV, +5.8%/yr 2026, stable across phases, high capacity. Don't use separately trained down models (DUAL_down or REL_down) as avoid overlays. The client's "both must accept" idea is best served by a separate market/exposure layer (R2_regime), evaluated against the market-dependent event rates quantified here. Judges should compare books averaged over signal-calendar phases, not single-phase holdout CAGRs.
lab_issues_found: MEDIUM: Sim results for a 20-name book depend on the signal-calendar phase. Shifting the start by 0-4 trading days moves 2026 CAGR by 10-14pp and DEV CAGR by 2-5pp; one phase-0 holdout result (DUAL vs RUP -8.9%/yr) was an extreme draw against a +3.0%/yr phase mean. Fix: S.compare should optionally average over start offsets 0..step-1 (equal-weight avoid overlays are phase-stable, under 1pp).

MEDIUM (method): the loss function alone (full-rank regression vs binary top-30% classifier on the same XR_neu label) moves DEV CAGR by about 4.6%/yr. Comparisons between labels must hold the loss fixed, or label effects get mis-attributed (DUAL looks better than XR_neu only because of this).

LOW: L.event_report's by_regime uses the signal-date regime, which barely moves outcome-conditioned labels (DUAL share 26.5-28.9% across regimes). The real dependence is on the realised market over the label window (DUAL +1 falls from 29.7% to 11.9%). Recommend reporting event rates split by same-window market return.
LOW: Sim's cash_yield defaults to 0. Mask-gated books that go to cash (e.g. a Nifty 500 > 200dma gate) are understated against a 6.5% cash alternative. The G_mkt200 numbers here use 0% cash.

NOTE: down-event classifiers trained on residual labels (AUC about 0.56 robust) do not make profitable avoid overlays on raw-return books in rebound regimes. The avoided names carry vol/beta exposure that paid in 2026 (+96bp vs +84bp universe per 20d).

refined.headline: Ensembling the relative label with an absolute barrier model and a trend-scan model adds no alpha. It adds a hidden regime bet. ENS3, an equal-weight rank average of XR_neu, the A2 barrier (h20, 3.0/1.5 ATR) and TSX trend-scan, won the pre-declared DEV selection with the highest DEV t: +15.4%/yr excess vs random, t 4.37, against 3.81 for XR alone. Paired against XR, though, it adds +0.1%/yr in DEV (t 0.06). In the 2026 holdout it lost -7.0%/yr vs random, with all 5 calendar phases and all 8 K x step cells negative; XR alone made +3.3%. The barrier and trend models put 30-87% of their gain importance in market/regime features. In 2026 they rotated into large, liquid, low-vol names while small and high-vol names led, and alpha after factors is about 0. Feature ablation: NSE delivery data is the only group that adds IC significantly in both windows (dIC -0.0064 DEV, -0.0135 in 2026 when removed). Factor attribution: XR's long edge is not low-vol or reversal. Alpha after factors is +14.1%/yr (t 3.33, R2 0.10), and a static factor composite earns only +2.0%/yr. The avoid side, by contrast, is largely a linear factor (idio-vol) effect, and factor-neutralising the score makes the avoid screen hold in 2026 (t 2.9-3.7).

key_findings: Reproducibility: my XR_neu label equals R2_rel's pct_neu (max diff 3e-8), and my BAR label equals R2_dual's. The XR_all and BAR_all OOS scores are bit-identical to R2_rel h20_neu_RANK and R2_dual M_BAR. My walk_forward2 copy (adds per-fold gain importance) is bit-identical to L.walk_forward2, and my per-date metrics reproduce L.xs_metrics exactly.

Primary statistics: phase-averaged excess vs a horizon-matched 5-seed random baseline (signal calendar shifted 0..step-1 days), with NW t lag 20. Phase-0 S.compare numbers are also reported. All 'dev_cagr' figures in the candidate list are phase-averaged; holdout CAGRs are annualised over Jan-Oct 2026.

Selection (pre-declared before any sim, DEV only): ENS3 won the long book (DEV t 4.37) and ENS_BT won the avoid screen (DEV t 4.33). 2026 exam: ENS3 -7.0%/yr vs random (FAIL); ENS_BT avoid +1.6%/yr (t 0.88, not significant).

No ensemble beats XR in a paired DEV test (ENS3 +0.1%/yr t 0.06; ENS_XT +0.3% t 0.13). In 2026 every ensemble and every absolute/trend model lags XR by 9-14%/yr (paired t -1.3 to -1.8). A higher DEV t can come from lower tracking variance rather than more return.

Mechanism: market/regime features carry 61%->87% of BAR's gain importance, 29%->57% of TSX's and 12%->19% of XR's across folds. In 2026 the BAR/TSX/ENS3 top-20 rotated into large, liquid, low-vol names (ENS3 vol pctile 0.38 vs 0.62 in DEV; turnover 0.83). 2026 factors were LOWVOL -18.9%/yr, LOWIDIO -22.9%, SIZE (small-big) +5.6%. Realised factor-neutral skill of the picks stayed positive (XR pct 0.517), so the losses came from the tilt. Removing market features cost DEV 3-11%/yr (in 8 of 9 model-years) and added 13-15%/yr in 2026. It is a factor-timing bet that paid in 2023-25 and failed in 2026.
Absolute barrier label: its whole DEV edge is regime timing. Without market features BAR's top-20 book is -1.8%/yr in DEV (picks' raw excess -12 bps per trade).

Feature ablation on XR_neu (drop one group, retrain): delivery is the only group with a significant IC contribution in both windows (dIC when removed -0.0064 DEV, NW t -4.99 / non-overlap -2.44; -0.0135 in 2026, NW t -3.68 / non-overlap -2.85). Its dIC is negative in every year 2023-2026. deliv_pct is the best single feature for the relative target (IC +0.044 DEV, +0.045 2026) and survives controls (partial IC +0.042, t 5.0). Book effect -2.1%/yr K20 (t -1.19) and -1.1%/yr avoid in 2026 (t -2.54). Verdict: NSE delivery data adds value, modestly but robustly.

Momentum, technicals, volume and the xs-rank copies are redundant for IC (|dIC| <= 0.002 DEV). Momentum still matters for the top tail: dropping it costs the K20 book -3.2%/yr DEV (t -1.70) and -4.4% in 2026. The xs-rank group is a pure duplicate for a per-date rank target. Market features: DEV dIC -0.0033 (n.s.); removing them raised 2026 IC by +0.028.

Factor attribution (factors built from U with the same Sim, phase-averaged): XR K20 DEV excess +15.2%/yr leaves alpha +14.1%/yr (t 3.33, R2 0.10) after SIZE/MOM/REV/LOWVOL/LOWBETA/MKT, and +12.6% (t 3.15) after adding LOWIDIO/TREND. The book is SHORT low-vol (t -3.4) and weakly long reversal (t +1.2). The edge is not just low-vol or reversal.

Score decomposition: a static 7-characteristic composite with XR's own DEV loadings reproduces XR's IC (0.059 vs 0.060), but only via the bottom tail (AUC_bot 0.561, AUC_top 0.500). Its K20 book earns +2.0%/yr (t 0.29). The factor-neutral residual keeps 85% of the long excess. So the avoid side is mostly a linear factor (high idio-vol) effect and the long side is model-specific.

The factor-neutralised avoid screen is the most robust practical output: DEV t 5.5-8.1 and 2026 +2.2-2.3%/yr (t 2.9-3.7) for XR/ENS3/TSX, versus 2026 t 0.4-0.8 for the raw scores. DEV alone prefers it.

No alpha source reduces drawdowns: K20 maxDD is -25% to -31% in DEV vs -29.7% for random. At 50 vs 80 bps the excess over random is identical (same turnover); only the absolute CAGR falls by about 4.5 pp/yr.

Variants: 12 walk-forward models, 11 derived scores (4 ensembles, ENS3_nomkt, 6 FN/FC decompositions), 102 distinct DEV strategy specs at 50 bps (46 main + 56 K x step), 10 label variants screened on event rates only, 7 formal candidates. Bonferroni one-sided 5% hurdle: 3.30 for this agent, 3.93 programme-wide (~1190 specs). ENS3 passed both at 4.37 and still failed the holdout.
refined.recommendation:
Label stack, from the alpha-source study:
(1) Primary selection label: XR_neu at h=20, used alone. Do not ensemble it with absolute (barrier) or market-excess (trend-scan) models. They add no paired DEV return, and they import a regime-conditional size/low-vol tilt that cost about 10%/yr in 2026.
(2) Keep market/regime features out of the stock-selection score. Market timing belongs to the regime/exposure layer, where it can be sized and evaluated explicitly. For XR, dropping them is DEV-neutral (-1.9%/yr, t -0.9).
(3) AVOID screen: drop the bottom 30% of a factor-neutralised model score (per-date residual on 7 characteristic ranks). It has the highest DEV t of any avoid variant and was the only one significant in 2026. Expect only about +2-3%/yr over the EW universe.
(4) Keep NSE delivery features: they are the only feature group with a significant every-year IC contribution.
(5) Drop the xs-rank duplicate features; this is neutral.
(6) Pre-register for fresh data, without promoting yet, because the 2026 evidence is holdout-informed: the factor-neutral long book and the no-market XR model.
(7) Drawdown control must come from the regime layer, since no alpha source reduced maxDD.
Judges should rely on paired difference tests between candidates, not on 'highest DEV t'.
lab_issues_found: MEDIUM (definition drift and model noise): R2_dual builds XR_neu with 0.5*beta_60+0.5 without clipping, while R2_rel, round-1 B_relative and R2_alpha clip beta_60 to [0,3] first. The labels barely differ (pct corr 0.99986; 0.47% of rows change 3-class), yet the trained OOS scores correlate only 0.973 (max abs diff 0.08). Score differences of that size are noise. Fix: put a canonical label builder in lablib.

LOW-MEDIUM (OLS neutralisation is not rank-neutral): the XR_neu pct still has per-date rank IC +0.030 (t 9.7) with log_turn20 and -0.032 (t -5.6) with vol_20, both OLS regressors. OLS removes the mean relation, but illiquid and high-vol names have more right-skewed returns and lower median residuals. The +1 class is therefore slightly more liquid and lower-vol than intended. Fix if exact neutrality matters: neutralise in rank space or within buckets.

MEDIUM (method): the Newey-West t (Bartlett, lag 20) of per-date IC differences on short windows of overlapping 20d forward returns overstates significance. For 2026, the same dIC gives NW t 5.45 vs non-overlap t 1.31. Report both or block-bootstrap by month; prefer paired daily-book tests, which have no forward-window overlap.

refined.headline: Timing the market does not reliably help, net of whipsaw. No point-in-time regime signal predicted the next-20-day market return consistently across 2021-22, 2023-25 and 2026, and all 9 walk-forward timing models scored below 0.5 AUC on DEV (0.39-0.47). The best DEV gate, breadth50>0.5, won in one episode (the 2025 drawdown) with null p=0.085, which fails multiple testing. It lost in 2021-22 and only broke even against always-invested in 2026 (EW book +0.6 pp CAGR, XR20 book -3.7 pp). The 200-dma rule cost about 20 pp of 2026 CAGR. The relative edge does not depend on the regime, so the regime layer should be a fixed exposure policy, not a timer.

key_findings: Absolute labels are mostly market. The between-date share of 20d return variance is 22.9% (18.5% for the 0/1 sign label). The daily +1 share of the sign label (6.5%..96.7% on DEV) has Pearson 0.875 (DEV) / 0.948 (2026) with the Nifty 500 next-20d return and 0.979 with the EW-universe return.

The market part was not forecastable here. Single-feature correlations flip sign between PRE 2021-22, DEV 2023-25 and 2026 (dist_sma200 rho -0.30 / +0.00 / -0.59; vix_rel +0.02 / +0.17 / +0.54). No feature keeps the same sign with |t|>2 in all three windows.

All 9 walk-forward timing models (logit and depth-2 LGBM x 3 targets) have DEV AUC below 0.5 (0.39-0.47), and their coefficients flip sign between folds. Of the 14 primary signals, only breadth50>0.5 (AUC 0.61 vs E0), mom60>0 (0.56) and the VOTE composite containing them (0.53) beat 0.5 on DEV. Only breadth beats the always-risk-on accuracy (0.622 vs 0.603).

Sleeve-level gating (scaling new sleeve entries; no extra trades; verified bit-identical to L.Sim) selected breadth50>0.5 with 0% risk-off on DEV. EW book: Sharpe_xs 0.32->0.77, CAGR 10.8%->15.6%, maxDD -28.9%->-12.9%. Circular-shift null p 0.085, which fails Bonferroni over 28 variants. The gain came from one episode (2025 -14.2%->+4.2%; 2024 13.3%->4.2%).

Out of sample the breadth gate is mixed. PRE 2021-22: EW -4.9 pp CAGR, Sharpe_xs -0.73, null p 0.915. 2026: it beat its random-timing null (p<0.005) but only broke even against always-in (EW +0.6 pp; XR20 -3.7 pp). The 200-dma rule changed 2026 CAGR by -20.3 pp (EW) and -23.7 pp (XR20).

Drawdown cuts are mostly mechanical. The lab Sim's raw Sharpe rewards holding cash: a static 55% EW mix lifts it from 0.67 to 0.91 with zero skill, while cash-adjusted Sharpe stays at 0.32. A coin-flip timer cuts DEV maxDD by 13.6 pp. Timers beat a static mix with the same exposure by only 4-8 pp of maxDD on DEV.

Whipsaw and implementation matter. In a noisy-oracle test, sleeve gating needs about 60% block accuracy for a reliable gain; a daily overlay paying 50 bps per round-trip switch needs about 70%. The same rule changes sign across implementations: the 200-dma rule is -1.0 pp as a gate and +3.2 pp as a daily overlay on DEV; breadth as pure index timing is -8.3 pp on DEV and +15.7 pp in 2026.

The relative edge is regime-independent. XR20 excess over random is +1.21% per 20d trade in up markets and +1.28% in down markets (slope t 0.39). No regime signal splits it (|t|<=1.02). Timing can only scale beta (XR20 beta to EW 1.03).

Parameter map: each rule family is stable inside a window and unstable across windows. Breadth is positive on DEV at every threshold 0.45-0.65 and negative in PRE at every threshold. mom60 is positive on DEV and negative in 2026 at every threshold. The 200-dma rule is about 0 on DEV and -7 to -20 pp in 2026 at every band. VIX is the mirror image.
Volatility targeting also fails: EW Sharpe_xs DEV -0.13 (null p 0.82), 2026 -0.36. 20-day index returns mean-reverted after stress in 2021-22 and 2026.

Variants: 14 primary signals x 2 risk-off levels = 28, plus 40 sensitivity-grid variants and 1 vol target = 69 distinct timing variants, evaluated as 222 book-level DEV specifications (sleeve gating on EW and XR20, daily overlay, index timing). Also 22 single-feature tests, 9 timing models and 1 XR_neu model. Costs (50/80 bps) and the 5 calendar phases are sensitivities, not variants.
refined.recommendation: Do not add a direction-timing regime layer to the label stack. Use a regime-free relative label as primary (XR_neu, or R2_rel's neumom); its edge is the same in up and down markets. Set gross exposure as a fixed, client-chosen policy: static de-risking leaves cash-adjusted Sharpe unchanged and cuts drawdown roughly in proportion. If a drawdown governor is required, the least-bad pre-registered option is breadth50<0.5 => 50% invested, applied only at each sleeve's own 20-day rebalance (no extra trades). On XR20 it changed CAGR by -1.3 pp (DEV) and -1.5 pp (2026) and improved maxDD by 10.8 / 8.0 pp. Treat it as insurance with uncertain, possibly negative, cost: it lost 4.4 pp against a static mix in 2021-22. Never use 200-dma or VIX trend filters (harmful in 2 of 3 windows; about -20 pp in 2026). Never model absolute direction labels per stock: their class mix is about 0.9 correlated with the unforecastable next-20d market. Judges should compare de-risked books on Sharpe in excess of cash, or against same-exposure static mixes, not on the Sim's raw Sharpe. Re-test the LOG4 'buy fear, avoid over-extension' logit on post-2026 data only.
lab_issues_found: L.Sim.run's 'sharpe' is not cash-adjusted, so books holding cash look better: a static 55% EW / 45% cash mix lifts the DEV Sharpe from 0.67 to 0.91 with no skill, while Sharpe in excess of 6.5% cash stays at 0.32. Compare de-risked or gated books on excess Sharpe or against same-exposure static mixes.

Benchmark mismatch: Nifty 500 is a price index while stock series are dividend-adjusted and the elig universe is small-cap heavy. In 2026 the EW-universe mean 20d return was +1.3% versus -0.5% for Nifty 500, and the N0 and E0 base rates were 51% vs 65%. A timer trained on the index target de-risks EW or small-cap books at the wrong times.
Sim sleeves that have not started yet hold un-yielding cash for the first 15 days of each window (an all-cash book earns 5.85%, not 6.5%, in the 2026 window). Minor, and the same for every variant.
Results depend on the signal-calendar phase (entry-day grid), so I averaged all metrics over 5 phases; null tests use phase 0. R2_rel saw the same effect.

The EW-universe target drops rows whose 20d window fails fw.ok (mean coverage 99.84%), so survivorship is negligible. No leakage found: per-date features are constant, the foresight canaries respond (+31 pp / -27 pp DEV CAGR), and the 22-day embargo holds.

refined.headline: R1dn capitulation reversal re-validates on lab v2, but only as a market-breadth (washout) effect. Event-weighted DEV excess is +57 bps/10d vs the same-date universe (t 6.2, passes Bonferroni over 720 tests), but day-weighted it is +16 bps (t 0.7): isolated breakdowns keep falling. Gated on >=5% of eligible names at new 20-day lows in a falling market (A1), the day-weighted excess is +36 bps (t 4.4), with 2026 holdout +64 bps (t 2.6). As an L.Sim sleeve (daily calendar, 20 slots/day, 13-22% exposure) it beats count-matched random stocks bought on the same days. That holds for all events (DEV t 2.4) and especially when events are ranked by a walk-forward relative meta-model: 10.4% CAGR, Sharpe 1.35, maxDD -9.6%, +4.4%/yr over all events (t 4.1), +7.0%/yr over matched random (t 4.7). In 2026 the edge over matched random survives (t 2.9), but the DEV-selected h=5 sleeve made only 0.4% absolute (h=10: 7.0%; Nifty 500 -9.9%). It adds nothing to the R2_rel relative core book: overlay 30.6% vs core 30.9% DEV, 13.8% vs 16.0% in 2026. None of the five other reversal families gives an investable long edge.

key_findings: Re-validation (lab v2, L.Sim, horizon-matched baselines): R1dn (close < prior 20d low, volz>1, Nifty-500 20d momentum<0) at h=10 has DEV event-weighted excess +57 bps vs the same-date universe (month-cluster t 6.22, Bonferroni-pass over 720 tests). Day-weighted it is only +16 bps (t 0.72); 2026 +76 bps event-weighted, -21 bps day-weighted. The edge lives on mass-breakdown days.

Breadth dose-response, the core structural fact: R1dn excess by share of the universe at new 20d lows (<2 / 2-5 / 5-10 / 10-20 / >=20%) is -20/+25/+42/+37/+82 bps in DEV and -112/-35/+19/+145/+97 bps in 2026. Isolated breakdowns and crashes continue; only market washouts reverse.

Breadth-gated gate A1 (close < prior 10d low, volz>0, mom20<0, >=5% of the universe at new 20d lows), chosen by a pre-declared DEV rule: DEV +38 bps event-weighted (t 4.35) and +36 bps day-weighted (t 4.36), both Bonferroni-pass; 2026 +64 bps (t 2.57); positive every year 2021-26. It fires on 16% of days with about 133 names per event day; 56 washout episodes in 2021-26.

Event rates move as expected with parameters. Volume>2 cuts events about 10x; L=40 fires 1.2x less than L=20; the breadth gate cuts event days from 35% to 13-16% but raises names per event day from about 26 to 100+. Event-weighted excess is positive in 264/270 R1 cells in DEV and 268/270 in 2026. Day-weighted excess depends on the market filter: negative with no filter, about 0 with mom20dn alone, median t 2.1-2.8 with breadth gates.

Sleeve investability (L.Sim step=1, 20 slots per daily sleeve, idle cash 0%) vs a count-matched universe random sleeve on the same days: A1 all events at h=10 makes DEV 4.3% vs 2.9% (t 2.37), 2026 4.8% vs 2.5% (t 1.35), maxDD -9.5%, exposure 14%. All 42 breadth-gated configs beat matched random in DEV and 2026, but none clears the portfolio-level Bonferroni hurdle (z 3.45 over 176 specs). S.compare's same-mask random arm cannot measure an event effect; a count-matched baseline is required.

Meta-labeling (walk_forward2 on 107k breakdown rows): within-event IC is 0.05-0.10 in DEV (t 3-7) and 0.03-0.055 in 2026 at h=5/10. Top-20 by the relative meta-score at h=5 makes DEV 10.4% (7.7% at 80 bps), Sharpe 1.35, maxDD -9.6%: +4.4%/yr over all events (t 4.09) and +7.0%/yr over matched random (t 4.70). R2_rel's every-bar relative model ranks events about as well, so no special model is needed. PIT thresholds and simple rules (depth, liquidity) fail.

The horizon depends on the regime. h=5 is best in DEV (fast V-rebounds in 2023-25 corrections) but made 0.4% in 2026; h=20 is weakest in DEV but made 11.6% in 2026 (drawn-out washouts). h=10 is the cost-robust compromise (DEV Sharpe at 130 bps 0.58 vs 0.49; 2026 7.0%). The lift over matched random holds at every h in 2026 (t 1.3-2.9).

Robustness of the meta sleeve: the edge survives a 1-day signal lag (DEV t 3.04 vs matched), both random entity halves (t 4.32 / 4.34), dropping the best month (t 4.32) and 130 bps costs at h=10. Quarterly excess is positive in 12/12 DEV quarters at h=10. t+1 entry bars are locked for only 0.07% of events. Capacity is about Rs 5-25 lakh per name (Rs 1 cr = median 5% of ADV).

Combination with the R2_rel core book (h20_neumom_RANK top-20, reproduced at 30.9% DEV): the sleeve adds nothing. Overlay (idle sleeve capital in the core) is below the core in DEV (t -0.7 to -3.1) and 2026 (13.5-15.3% vs 16.0%). Tilting the core toward gate events loses 1.0%/yr. The core already holds 25% gate events on gate days vs a 13% base share. Daily correlation with the core is 0.57-0.86 (both long a falling market); excess correlation is 0.08-0.41. MIX20 vs 80% core + 20% cash: +0.3 to +2.0% DEV, -0.4 to +2.1% 2026.

Other overreaction events (Bonferroni over 720 tests): crash days and recovered gap-downs continue when the market is quiet (DEV -130 to -250 bps, t up to -6.0, Bonferroni-pass), but this faded in 2026 (-28 bps) and excluding them did not help the core in DEV (t -0.52). Oversold RSI<20 in a falling market passes at h=5 as an event but loses as a sleeve in 2026 (-10.5%). 5-day losers and 52-week lows on volume show no edge. Upside blow-offs are a weak avoid hint (-65 bps in 2026, not Bonferroni in DEV).

Variants: 538 in total. 360 event-study cells x 2 statistics = 720 tests (Bonferroni |z| 3.98); 176 distinct DEV portfolio specs (one-sided z 3.45); 2 new walk-forward models (WF_R10, WF_A10) plus 2 reused R2_rel OOS scores. 2026 was printed beside DEV in every table, and all selections used DEV only. The h=10 recommendation over the DEV-best h=5 is a flagged post-holdout judgment call.
lab_issues_found: MEDIUM: S.compare draws its random arm from the same mask. On a sparse event mask it measures only the ranking within events, never the event effect itself. Event sleeves need a count-matched universe baseline (same days, same number of names). This was implemented as matched_mask in R2_event/common.py; suggest adding a baseline_mask / count-matching option to Sim.compare.

LOW: Sim.run ends its window at the last signal plus one period, so daily series from different (h, step) configs have different lengths (741 vs 743 DEV days). Combining books requires date alignment.

DESIGN: with step=1 and slot sizing, a sleeve can deploy at most 1/h of capital per day. A mass-capitulation day cannot be sized up beyond that, which structurally caps event-sleeve exposure (13-22% here).

MEDIUM: xs_metrics needs >= 30 rows per date, so event masks count only mass days. Its non-overlap subsample takes every h-th available date, which is not calendar non-overlap when event dates cluster, so its t-stats are erratic (e.g. 0.71 vs month-cluster 5.19 for the same IC). Use month-cluster t for event masks.
LOW: walk_forward2 default LightGBM params (num_leaves 31, min_child_samples 400) are too coarse for event-row training sets of 20-60k rows; pass smaller params (15 / 100 used here).
NOTE: L.Sim is reproduced bit-identically by the SimX subclass (copied run() plus a daily invested-fraction output), and R2_rel's core book reproduces exactly (30.88% DEV).
refined.recommendation: Event-sleeve slot of the label stack: use the breadth-gated capitulation label E2/A1. The gate is close < prior 10-day low, volz_20 > 0, Nifty-500 20d momentum < 0, and >= 5% of eligible names closing below their prior 20-day low. Rank the gated names with the relative model (R2_rel's every-bar neumom score or the WF_R10 meta-score; they are interchangeable) and buy the top 20 per event day at the next open. Each position gets 1/(20h) of the sleeve. Hold h=10 days with a time exit and no stops. h=5 was DEV-best at 50/80 bps, but h=10 is more cost-robust; that choice is a flagged judgment call. Fund it only from capital that is NOT already in the relative core book, such as a cash buffer or a separate low-exposure sleeve. Do not overlay it on, or tilt, a fully invested relative book: that adds nothing (the core already leans into washout names and is long the same market). Expected profile: about 5-10% CAGR on sleeve capital at 13-22% exposure, maxDD about 5-10%, lumpy (56 episodes in 5.75 years), mid/small-cap, capacity about Rs 5-25 lakh per name. Label-design facts for the judges: (1) buy washouts, never isolated breakdowns or crashes, which continue; (2) report event labels day-weighted as well as event-weighted, because event-weighted stats overstate sparse gates; (3) the quiet-day crash continuation is real in DEV but faded in 2026 and gave no portfolio benefit, so keep it out of the avoid layer for now. Confidence: medium-high that the washout excess is real (Bonferroni-pass, every year, holdout positive); low-medium that a separate sleeve adds money beyond the relative core.

judges.primary_selection_label: XR_neumom h=20 continuous residual rank. For signal date t and rows in U_t = elig_base_t, compute r = close[t+20]/open[t+1] - 1 on CA-adjusted prices; r is NaN where fw.ok(20) fails, never 0. Winsorise r at the per-date 1st/99th percentiles over U_t. Run a per-date OLS over U_t of r_w on [1, 0.5*clip(beta_60,0,3)+0.5, vol_20, log_turn20, mom_12_1 (NaN -> that date's median)]. The label is y = per-date percentile rank of the residual, in (0,1]. Reporting classes: +1 if y>0.7, -1 if y<=0.3, else 0 (exactly 30/40/30 on every date). Model: LightGBM regression on y-0.5 via walk_forward2 (yearly expanding refit, embargo 22 days, 52 PIT features, delivery features kept). Book: each week buy the top 20 by score among elig_base into 1 of 4 staggered sleeves (slot weight 1.25%, about 80 positions; K 10-30 per sleeve is a smooth plateau). Use liq2, or switch to liq5 above about Rs 25 cr AUM. Why RANK and not C20/T30/RUP: on DEV they are a statistical tie. Paired vs RANK, phase-averaged: C20 +2.7%/yr (t 1.3), T30 +3.9% (t 1.2), RUP +3.6% (t 1.0). The tie-break is a PM one. RANK has no cut parameter, so no cliff (T10/T20/T50 and B30 are cliffs). It has the lowest factor R2 (0.05) and the best IC (t 8.6). One score serves both the buy side and the avoid side. Its picks are the most liquid of the three. The DEV edge of the tail forms after factors equals RANK's: alpha +17.4% vs +17.8-18.0%.
judges.avoid_label: Use the -1 class of the same label: y<=0.3, the bottom 30% of the neumom h=20 residual rank. The operational avoid list is the bottom 10-30% of today's primary RANK score (10% for a tight veto). It is a veto list: never buy these names, and flag them inside discretionary or legacy holdings. It is NOT a short: the cash segment cannot carry overnight shorts, and round-1 F&O shorts lost about 20%/yr. Inside a top-20 book on the same score the avoid list is already excluded by construction. Value as an overlay (EW universe minus bottom 30%, phase-averaged): DEV +3.4%/yr (t 3.6, 5/5 phases), factor-adjusted +3.1% (t 5.0). 2026: +1.2% raw (t 0.8; a big-cap tilt in a small-cap year), factor-adjusted +2.5% (t 3.7). Do NOT train a dedicated down classifier. B30, DUAL_down and REL_down learn volatility (score corr -0.73 with idio-vol) and failed as overlays in 2026 (-2.0 to -2.7%/yr, 0/5 phases). Pre-registered refinement, not selected now: rank the avoid list on the factor-neutralised score (FN: per-date residual on 7 characteristic ranks). DEV prefers it on t (5.55), and it was steadier in 2026 (+2.3%, t 2.9), but it was built post hoc. If the client trades only F&O names, re-rank inside that universe: there the full-universe label is 29.5/45/25.5, not 30/40/30.
judges.regime_layer: None as a return source. Set gross exposure as a fixed policy from the client's drawdown budget: 100%, or a static 70-80% with the rest in a liquid fund. Static de-risking keeps the cash-adjusted Sharpe and cuts drawdown in proportion. Evidence: the relative excess does not depend on the regime (+1.21% per trade in up markets vs +1.28% in down; slope t 0.39). All 9 walk-forward timing models are anti-predictive on DEV (AUC 0.39-0.47). Every rule family flips sign across PRE / DEV / 2026, and the 200-dma rule cost about 20-24 pp of CAGR in 2026. Do not use 200-dma, VIX, 60d momentum, a vote of these, vol-targeting or ML timers. If the client insists on a governor, the only pre-registrable one is breadth50<0.5 -> 50% invested, applied only at the sleeve's own rebalance (no extra trades). On XR20 it cost -1.3 pp CAGR and gained +10.8 pp maxDD on DEV, and -1.5 pp / +8.0 pp in 2026. Against a static mix with the same exposure it was +3.2 / -0.0 pp, and it lost on the EW book in PRE 2021-22. Its null p is 0.09, so it fails multiple testing. Treat it as insurance with uncertain and possibly negative cost, not alpha.
judges.event_sleeve: None in the stack. The breadth-gated capitulation reversal (A1: close < prior 10d low, volz>0, N500 20d mom<0, >=5% of names at new 20d lows; top 20 events by the relative model) is a real effect: DEV +7.0%/yr vs count-matched random (t 4.7), 2026 t 2.9. As money it is small and awkward. It runs at 13-22% exposure, which gives a 4-10% CAGR sleeve. Capacity is about Rs 5-25 lakh per name on panic days with wide spreads. The best horizon flips with the regime: h=5 was best on DEV but made 0.4% in 2026. It is episodic: 56 washouts in 5.75 years, and the top 5 months carry about 58% of the excess. When active it correlates 0.78 with the core. Adding it lowers the combined book: overlay 30.6% vs core 30.9% on DEV, 13.8% vs 16.0% in 2026. At most it is an optional research sleeve for a static cash buffer (+0.3 to +2%/yr on 20% of capital). Keep the descriptive rule for discretionary use: washouts revert, isolated breakdowns keep falling. Do not buy single-name breakdowns on quiet days.
judges.horizon_and_exit: Hold 20 trading days. The signal is formed at close t. Enter at open t+1; books above about Rs 10 cr should work the order over day 1 at VWAP, which my check found costs about 1.4%/yr of excess (DEV +16.0% -> +14.6%, t 3.9). Exit at the close of the 20th bar with a pure time exit: no stops, targets or ATR trails (round 1 showed they destroy value). Forced exit at the last valid close on suspension or label_block. Cadence: each week one of 4 staggered sleeves (20 names each) turns over fully. Spread entries across the days of the week where operationally possible, because a single weekly calendar moved 2026 excess between -2% and +9%. That is about 12.6 round trips a year, roughly 6.3%/yr of cost at 50 bps; each extra 10 bps costs about 1.3%/yr of CAGR (excess vs random unchanged). Use 50 bps as the central cost: my tiered estimate for these picks (F&O 30 / mid 50 / small 95 bps) is 53 bps DEV and 47 bps 2026, against 56 bps for the universe. Stress at 80 bps. Retrain once a year on an expanding window. h=10 has more raw skill but is cost-bound (DEV 80 bps CAGR 16.2%, 130 bps 2.6%). h=15 sits in between. Training horizon barely matters when the hold is 20 days.

- Excess +2.3 to +5.3%/yr (t 0.35-0.81). Positive in sign, not significant. The quoted single-phase +9.2% was the luckiest of 5 phases.

ranking.reason: Primary. Simplest parameter-free encoding of the relative label. Phase-averaged DEV +16.5%/yr vs the seed-free EW book (t 4.5); every DEV year positive (+17.5/+34.5/+8.0 pp). DEV alpha after 6 factors +17.4% (t 4.0, R2 0.05); best IC (t 8.6), no 2026 decay. Picks more liquid than the universe (tiered cost 47-53 bps). judges.primary_selection_label:
XR_neumom, h=20, continuous residual rank (R2_rel h20_neumom_RANK).

Construction, for each signal date t:
- Return: r = open[t+1] -> close[t+20] on CA-adjusted prices. NaN unless fw.ok(20); never set to 0.
- Cross-section: V_t = elig_base rows with finite r.
- Winsorise r per date at the 1st/99th percentile over V_t.
- Per-date OLS over V_t of the winsorised r on [1, 0.5*clip(beta_60,0,3)+0.5, vol_20, log_turn20, mom_12_1]. Missing mom_12_1 is filled with that date's median.
- Label y = per-date percentile rank of the residual over V_t, in (0,1].
- Model: LightGBM regression on y-0.5 via L.walk_forward2 (yearly expanding folds 2023-26, embargo 22 days, the 52 PIT features including NSE delivery). Out-of-sample scores only.
- Action: long the top-20 names by score.

Why this one:
- It won R2_rel's composite rule, which was declared before the last six models were trained and uses DEV data only.
- It has no cut parameter, the lowest factor loading (R2 0.05), the most stable IC (DEV 0.064, 2026 0.061), and one score serves both the buy side and the avoid side.

Statistical caveats on the choice:
- neu (the same regression without the mom_12_1 regressor) is indistinguishable: paired DEV +0.5%/yr (t 0.24), 2026 +0.6%. It is an acceptable substitute.
- DEV data cannot separate RANK from C20 or T30. T30 minus RANK is +3.9%/yr on DEV (t 1.2-1.7). That is inside model noise: two near-identical labels moved books by ±3%/yr per year. Two of R2_rel's seven criteria used phase-0 statistics, where RANK had its luckiest of five phases.
- RANK wins on complexity, not on evidence. Pre-register a RANK+T30 rank blend as the challenger, to be scored only on data after 2026-10-14.
judges.avoid_label:
The bottom 30% of the same h20_neumom_RANK score on date t. 30% was pre-declared; the DEV plateau runs from 10% to 50% (phase-averaged t 3.2-3.8).

How to use it:
- Never buy or keep holding those names.
- The overlay version is equal-weight elig_base minus those names, rebalanced every 5 days, held 20 days.
- It is an avoid/exit signal, not a short. F&O shorts lost money in round 1, and the -1 class is under-represented among F&O names (25.5%).

Performance vs the equal-weight universe:
- DEV +3.4%/yr (NW t 3.6; 90% block-bootstrap CI +1.8% to +4.9%; 11/12 quarters positive).
- 2026 +1.2% (t 0.9).
- After factor adjustment, alpha is +2.5% to +3.1%/yr (t 3.7-5.0) in both windows.

Rejected alternatives:
- Dedicated down classifiers (B30, DUAL_down, REL_down). They learn volatility and lost 2-3%/yr as overlays in 2026.
- The lowest-P(top30) screen (R2_dual AVOID_RUPup). On DEV it has the same mean (+3.4%) with lower tracking error. But it drops low-vol names that are unlikely winners, not predicted losers: its AUC on the -1 class is 0.49. Its 2026 +6% came from the vol factor (factor alpha about +2.6%), so R2_dual's "strong" verdict leans on the holdout.
- The factor-neutralised avoid (R2_alpha FN). Built after the fact; its higher DEV t comes from lower tracking error on a smaller mean (+2.3%). Pre-register it instead.
- Do not move the cut to 10% because it looked most robust in 2026. That would be selecting on the holdout.
judges.regime_layer:
None as a return source. Hold a fixed gross exposure chosen by the client: 100%, or a static 70-80% if drawdown tolerance requires it. A static mix keeps the cash-adjusted Sharpe and cuts maxDD roughly in proportion.

Statistical basis:
- The best DEV gate (breadth50 > 0.5) has a circular-shift null p of 0.085 as a single test, among 28 primary variants. A Bonferroni pass would need p < 0.0018.
- That gate's DEV gain is one episode (2025). It is negative in PRE 2021-22 at every threshold and only breaks even in 2026.
- All 9 walk-forward timers have DEV AUC 0.39-0.47, and their coefficients flip sign between folds.
- DEV holds only about 37 independent 20-day market observations.
- The relative edge does not depend on the regime: +1.21% vs +1.28% per trade in up vs down markets (slope t 0.39). A timer can only scale beta.
- Never use 200-dma or VIX filters: they cost 20-24 pp of CAGR in 2026.
- A breadth rule that cuts to 50% invested is at most optional insurance with an uncertain, possibly negative, cost. It is not part of the label stack.
judges.event_sleeve:
None in the core stack.

The breadth-gated capitulation effect (A1: close below the prior 10-day low, volz > 0, Nifty-500 20-day momentum < 0, and at least 5% of the universe at new 20-day lows) is a genuine event-study fact:
- Day-weighted t: PRE 2.4, DEV 4.4, 2026 2.3.
- It passes Bonferroni across 720 tests on DEV.

As an investable sleeve it is not established:
- It rests on about 30 DEV washout episodes, and the top 5 months carry 58% of the excess.
- Exposure is only 13-22%.
- The best horizon depends on the regime: h=5 on DEV, h=20 in 2026. The DEV-selected h=5 version made 0.4% absolute in 2026.
- Added to the fully invested core, it lowers return in both windows: 30.6% vs 30.9% on DEV, 13.8% vs 16.0% in 2026.

At most, run it as a pre-registered paper trade for idle cash only: A1 gate, events ranked by the core score, h=10. Note that the h=10 choice was made after 2026 was visible.
judges.horizon_and_exit:
Hold 20 trading days.
- Signal at close t; enter at open t+1; exit on time at the close of the 20th bar.
- No stops, targets or trailing stops (round 1 showed they destroy value).
- Stagger entries: at least weekly (step 5, 4 sleeves of 20 names), ideally daily. A single calendar phase moved 2026 excess from -2.0% to +9.2% and the DEV t from 3.2 to 4.25.
- K=20 names per sleeve (K=10-50 is a smooth plateau).
- Universe: liq2 (Rs 2 cr 20-day turnover). liq5 is the capacity case; its edge is smaller (phase-0 DEV +14.3% vs +19.1%).
- Costs: 50 bps central, 80 and 130 bps stress. Each extra 10 bps costs about 1.5%/yr of absolute CAGR; the excess over random is nearly cost-invariant.
- If a name is still in the top 20 at its sleeve's rebalance, keep it. The simulator charges a full round trip, so live costs are slightly lower.
- Do not add an early exit when a held name falls into the avoid tail. That rule is untested.

Why h=20: h=10 has the most raw skill, but its horizon-matched random baseline is about 1% CAGR at 50 bps. DEV CAGR at 80 bps is 16.2% / 19.6% / 25.2% for h = 10 / 15 / 20.

Deflation. Programme size is about 1,600-1,700 portfolio specs (round 1 about 520-600, round 2 about 1,100) plus about 720 event-study tests. Over R2_rel's 272 long-book excess series (mean correlation 0.40), the Li-Ji effective trial count is 71 (Nyholt 210). With a null t sd of 1.10, the expected maximum null t is 2.9-3.3 for N_eff 150-300. The selected spec's deflated Sharpe is 0.80-0.86, or 0.68-0.75 using the lag-120 t of 3.69, below the 0.95 bar. Family-level DEV skill clearly passes: 73% of 429 DEV specs have t > 2 and 38% have t > 3. The spec-level magnitude does not.

2026 sits below the DEV magnitude. The 2026 phase-averaged 90% CI is -3.3% to +11.6% (60-day blocks), which excludes the DEV point estimate of +15.8%; the DEV-minus-2026 gap has z of about 1.9. IC did not decay (0.064 to 0.061). The shortfall is weak conversion on the long side (top-30 AUC 0.508) plus factor headwinds: the book is short trend and momentum, and momentum returned +26% in 2026. The DEV excess also leans on 2024 (+27.6%); without 2024 it is +9.7%.

Model noise is as large as the variant differences. Near-identical labels (clipped vs unclipped beta, label corr 0.99986) gave books differing by +3.3 / +1.0 / -2.8%/yr by year, and -1.6% in 2026. neumom vs neu and RANK vs C20 vs T30 are all inside that band, so DEV does not identify the label form.

Holdout contamination. Round 1 reported 2026, and that shaped the round-2 design: the relative focus and the lab-v2 fixes. So 2026 is not a clean test of the relative-vs-absolute decision. Several round-2 recommendations were informed by 2026: R2_event's h=10, R2_alpha's FN and no-market variants, R2_rel's 10% avoid cut, and R2_dual's 'strong' AVOID_RUPup. Only data after 2026-10-14 is a clean exam.

DEV t is a poor selector across families. R2_alpha's pre-declared winner ENS3 (DEV t 4.37) failed 2026 at -7%/yr; its high t came from low tracking variance. Across 22 candidates, DEV t predicts 2026 weakly (Spearman 0.37) and DEV excess does better (0.73). Structural regime-freeness was the best predictor of holdout survival.

Effective sample is small. DEV is 3 years, 36 months and about 37 independent 20-day market windows. Yearly excess ranged +8% to +28%, so uncertainty at the year level is larger than the Newey-West t suggests.

Relative is not absolute. P(net>0 | +1) is 90% overall but 38% in the worst month. The label identifies stocks that beat their peers, not stocks that will rise. The market component (23% of 20-day return variance) was not forecastable here, and the book has no drawdown protection: its maxDD is about the same as random's (about -27% to -30% on DEV).

Costs and capacity. The edge concentrates in liq2 small and mid caps. At liq5, phase-0 excess is DEV +14.3% (vs +19.1%) and 2026 +4.6% (vs +9.2%). At a Rs 25 cr book, 8.5% of orders exceed 10% of ADV. Real all-in costs for small caps can exceed 80 bps.

The avoid side is largely factor-explained: R2 0.58-0.71, loading on high idio-vol and small size. Its raw excess therefore swings with those factors (2026 +1.2% raw vs +2.5% factor alpha). A plain 12-1 momentum avoid filter matched it on DEV (+3.7%, t 3.1).

Checked and cleared: the simulator exits at the last valid close before a label_block row or segment break. For the selected book this happened in 11 + 1 of 2,900 DEV trades and 0 of 700 in 2026. The DEV excess is also robust to dependence: NW lag 20-120 gives t 3.7-4.1, and block bootstraps of 20-120 days give p < 0.001.

devil.final_recommendation:
The label survives: XR_neumom h=20 continuous residual rank, long top-20, with the bottom-30% avoid list. It reproduces exactly from independent code, carries no leakage, generalises across entity halves (even with half-trained models), is not a simple factor tilt (factor-adjusted DEV alpha +17.7%, t 4.5), and is smooth across K, step, cost and lag. The judges' stack, with no regime layer and no event sleeve, should stand. It survives only with these caveats:

1. Planning numbers. Plan on about +5%/yr excess over the equal-weight universe or random (range 0-10%), not DEV's +16%. 2026 shows intact IC but no measurable long-book profit: seed ensemble -0.2%/yr. Multiple testing at N about 2,000 leaves DSR 0.63-0.76, and the Bonferroni-haircut excess is +6.7%.
2. Execution. Ship a 3+ seed rank ensemble and stagger entries daily or weekly; never report a single seed and phase. Trade at the next open with no delay: each day of delay costs about 1.9 pp/yr.
3. Capacity. Hard limit of about Rs 25 lakh per name (about Rs 20 cr AUM), with a participation cap of 5% of 20-day median ADV. Switch to liq5 above that. Rs 1 Cr per name is not viable: DEV CAGR falls to 6-18% depending on the impact coefficient Y.
4. Avoid veto. Treat the avoid veto (+3.4% DEV, +0.9 to +1.7% in 2026 across all perturbations) as the most reliable component.
5. Kill rule. Pre-register a paper or small-size live period of at least 6 months (about 25 weekly cohorts) before scaling. Kill or review if rolling 6-month excess vs random falls below -5%, or if the IC drops below 0.02.
6. Unknown remaining edge. Disclose that the book is short momentum and long liquidity by construction, so momentum-led small-cap rallies like 2026 will look bad on a relative basis.
